lines.say: This man looks deep in prayer,
but he may not be alive.
This is Saint Francis of Assisi in His Tomb,
painted by Francisco de Zurbarán.
Most people see a friar praying
over a human skull.
The painting belongs to the Milwaukee Art Museum.
And the picture seems to agree.
His hands hold the skull,
and one bare foot steps forward.
But look at the hood.
His face has almost vanished into shadow.
According to a tradition popular in the seventeenth century,
a pope opened Francis's tomb at Assisi.
He found the body miraculously preserved,
standing upright in the tomb.
Zurbarán painted that vision
for the Count Duke of Olivares.
He isn't a monk at prayer.
He's a dead saint,
still standing in his grave.
So is he praying,
or has he been standing there for centuries?
